newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: UOB Bank has not plans to merge listings.
newsitem.headline: UOB Bank has not plans to merge listings.

text.p: Singapore's United Overseas Bank Ltd (UOB) said on Friday it had no plans at present to merge the local and foreign listings of its shares.
A bank statement gave no other details.

The statement followed a day of hectic trading on the Stock Exchange of Singapore in which the local and foreign share tranches of big Singapore companies converged on rumours that the government might abolish the practice of dual listings.
Dual listings were introduced in the early 1990s to protect companies which were considered of strategic importance to Singapore from takeover or undue influence by foreigners.

Some well-known Singapore companies, including all four of the big banks Development Bank of Singapore, Oversea Chinese Banking Corp, Overseas Union Bank and United Overseas Bank, Singapore Airlines, and the monopoly publisher Singapore Press, have split listings.
The local tranches can only be bought by Singaporeans or Singapore companies. Foreign tranches can be bought by anyone.
Foreign tranches traditionally hold a premium over local tranches and tend to be much more volatile. Scrapping the split between the tranches would remove this price differential.

Dealers said there was a growing expectation that the distinction between the tranches might erode and could possibly be scrapped. Several dealers say they have advised clients to anticipate such a move.
UOB's foreign share fell 60 cents on Friday to Singapore $12.30 while its local share rose 45 cents to S$9.60.
